title: Module A Mock Test: Survey of English Literature

questions.q: Which member of the University Wits is famous for introducing blank verse to the English stage, a technique Ben Jonson called his 'mighty line'?
questions.explanation: Christopher Marlowe popularized blank verse in plays like Doctor Faustus.

questions.q: To whom did William Shakespeare dedicate the first 126 of his sonnets?
questions.explanation: Sonnets 1-126 are addressed to a young aristocrat known as the Fair Youth.

questions.q: In Edmund Spenser's 'The Faerie Queene', what virtue does the Redcrosse Knight represent?
questions.explanation: The Redcrosse Knight is the patron of Holiness in Book I.

questions.q: Who coined the term 'Metaphysical Poets' to describe John Donne and his followers?
questions.explanation: Dr. Samuel Johnson coined the term in his Lives of the Poets.

questions.q: What is the explicitly stated purpose of John Milton's 'Paradise Lost'?
options: To chronicle the fall of Satan
To justify the ways of God to men
To explain the origins of the universe
questions.explanation: Milton states this purpose in the opening lines of Book 1.

questions.q: Ben Jonson popularized which theatrical genre, based on the medieval medical theory of four bodily fluids?
questions.explanation: The Comedy of Humours features characters driven by a single dominant trait.

questions.q: Who was appointed as England's first official Poet Laureate in 1668?
questions.explanation: John Dryden received the first official royal patent for Poet Laureate.

questions.q: Alexander Pope's 'The Rape of the Lock' is best classified as which type of poem?
questions.explanation: It treats the trivial theft of a lock of hair with grandiose epic conventions.

questions.q: Jonathan Swift's 'A Modest Proposal' uses savage irony to suggest solving Irish poverty by doing what?
options: Selling children as food for the rich
questions.explanation: It highlights the cruelty of British landlords through an outrageous, satirical proposal.

questions.q: Which author is credited with inventing the Epistolary Novel (a novel written as a series of letters)?
questions.explanation: Richardson wrote Pamela and Clarissa entirely in the form of letters.

questions.q: The publication of which book in 1798 officially launched the Romantic movement in England?
questions.explanation: Lyrical Ballads was published jointly by Wordsworth and Coleridge.

questions.q: Who defined poetry as 'the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings'?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth wrote this in the Preface to the Lyrical Ballads.

questions.q: Samuel Taylor Coleridge coined the phrase 'willing suspension of disbelief' in which of his works?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
questions.explanation: It appears in his major work of literary criticism, Biographia Literaria.

questions.q: Percy Bysshe Shelley's 'Adonais' is a pastoral elegy written to mourn the death of which fellow poet?
questions.explanation: Shelley wrote it after Keats died of tuberculosis at age 25.

questions.q: Which Victorian poet perfected the form of the 'Dramatic Monologue', as seen in 'My Last Duchess'?
questions.explanation: Browning used this form to explore the dark psychology of his characters.

questions.q: Alfred, Lord Tennyson's massive elegy 'In Memoriam' explores Victorian doubts regarding science and faith after the death of:
questions.explanation: He wrote it to mourn his close Cambridge friend, A.H.H.

questions.q: The fictional, semi-mythical region of 'Wessex' serves as the primary setting for the pessimistic novels of which author?
questions.explanation: Hardy based Wessex on the real counties of southwestern England.

questions.q: Which novel by Charles Dickens begins with the famous line 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times'?
questions.explanation: It is the opening line of his novel set during the French Revolution.

questions.q: In what year were both T.S. Eliot's 'The Waste Land' and James Joyce's 'Ulysses' published?
questions.explanation: 1922 is considered the 'miracle year' of literary Modernism.

questions.q: The revolutionary narrative technique used by Virginia Woolf and James Joyce to mimic the continuous, chaotic flow of a character's internal thoughts is called:
questions.explanation: Stream of Consciousness breaks traditional syntax to replicate raw thought.

questions.q: The famous lines 'Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold' appear in which prophetic poem by W.B. Yeats?
questions.explanation: This poem envisions the breakdown of society after World War I.

questions.q: Samuel Beckett's 'Waiting for Godot' is the defining masterpiece of which post-WWII theatrical movement?
questions.explanation: Absurdist theatre strips away traditional plot to reflect existential meaninglessness.

questions.q: The famous line 'All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others' appears in which allegorical novella?
questions.explanation: It is the ultimate corrupted commandment in George Orwell's 'Animal Farm'.

questions.q: William Golding's 'Lord of the Flies' primarily argues that:
options: There is an inherent darkness and savagery in human nature
Civilization will always triumph over chaos
questions.explanation: The stranded boys quickly shed civilization and resort to murder.

questions.q: Which novel by Salman Rushdie uses 'Magic Realism' to link the lives of telepathic children to the history of independent India?
questions.explanation: Midnight's Children uses magic realism to tell the story of India.
